breaches.records_note: About 87 million users' profile data harvested via a third-party app
breaches.what_happened: The FTC found that Facebook violated a 2012 consent order by deceiving users about their control over personal information, after a third-party app harvested profile data from about 87 million users and shared it with Cambridge Analytica. The settlement also imposed a 20-year consent decree with new privacy oversight requirements.

breaches.cost_type: Total 2024 financial impact reported in year-end earnings ($2.2B direct response plus $867M business disruption)
breaches.records_note: Up to 190 million individuals, per UnitedHealth's updated disclosure
breaches.source_name: Becker's Hospital Review (citing UnitedHealth year-end earnings)
breaches.what_happened: Ransomware group ALPHV/BlackCat breached Change Healthcare in February 2024, forcing UnitedHealth to take claims processing systems offline for weeks and disrupting payments across the US healthcare system. UnitedHealth paid a $22 million ransom and later reported the breach potentially affected 190 million individuals, the largest healthcare breach ever reported to federal regulators.

breaches.records_note: About 76 million current, former, and prospective customers
breaches.what_happened: A hacker infiltrated T-Mobile's systems and stole sensitive data on current, former, and prospective customers, including names, Social Security numbers, and driver's license data. T-Mobile agreed to settle the resulting class action litigation without admitting wrongdoing and committed an additional $150 million to data security improvements.

breaches.records_note: About 98 million individuals in the US, per settlement coverage
breaches.what_happened: A former cloud provider employee exploited a misconfigured firewall on Capital One's cloud infrastructure and downloaded roughly 30GB of data spanning more than a decade of credit card applications. The breach went undetected for months and led to a $190 million class action settlement plus an $80 million OCC fine for cloud risk management failures.

breaches.cost_type: Negative Q3 2023 earnings impact disclosed in SEC Form 8-K (plus under $10M in one-time response costs)
breaches.records_note: Personal data of customers who used MGM services before March 2019; total count not disclosed
breaches.what_happened: Attackers linked to the Scattered Spider group used social engineering against an IT help desk to gain access, then encrypted systems across MGM's Las Vegas and regional properties. MGM shut down systems to contain the damage, disrupting slot machines, reservations, and hotel operations for days, and declined to pay the ransom.

breaches.cost_type: Multistate settlement with 50 attorneys general (October 2024); parallel FTC settlement
breaches.records_note: 131.5 million US guest records, per state attorneys general
breaches.what_happened: Intruders had undetected access to the Starwood guest reservation database from July 2014 until September 2018, including after Marriott acquired Starwood in 2016 and took control of its network. The breach exposed 131.5 million US guest records, and 50 state attorneys general alleged Marriott failed to implement reasonable data security during the Starwood integration.

breaches.cost_type: Joint multistate settlement with 49 attorneys general (2023); separate $3M SEC settlement for misleading disclosures
breaches.records_note: Donor data of more than 13,000 customer organizations across the US, Canada, UK, and Netherlands; individual count not disclosed
breaches.what_happened: A ransomware attack on cloud software provider Blackbaud exposed donor data belonging to more than 13,000 customer organizations, including bank account information and Social Security numbers. The SEC later charged the company with misleading investors about the scope of the attack, and 49 state attorneys general reached a separate joint settlement.

breaches.cost_type: Ransom payment reported by Bloomberg sources; company did not confirm the figure
breaches.records_note: More than 75,000 people, per SEC filings
breaches.what_happened: A ransomware attack using Phoenix Locker malware disrupted CNA's network for weeks in March 2021, locking employees out of corporate email and other systems. The company reportedly paid the attackers about two weeks after the intrusion to regain control of its systems, one of the largest disclosed ransom payments at the time.

breaches.cost_type: Class action settlement agreed September 2024 (later moved into bankruptcy proceedings)
breaches.records_note: 6.9 million users via the DNA Relatives feature
breaches.what_happened: Attackers used credential stuffing with passwords leaked from other breaches to access about 14,000 accounts, then scraped data shared through the DNA Relatives feature, ultimately exposing 6.9 million users' genetic and profile data. The company had offered multi-factor authentication but did not require it until after the breach.

breaches.cost_label: $26 million (approx; £20 million ICO fine converted at ~1.30)
breaches.cost_type: UK ICO GDPR penalty (October 2020), reduced from an initial £183.39 million notice
breaches.records_note: About 429,612 customers and staff, per the ICO investigation
breaches.what_happened: Attackers linked to the Magecart group compromised British Airways' payment pages with skimming code that copied customer card data to an attacker-controlled site while bookings completed normally. The UK ICO found the airline had been logging some payment card data in plaintext and failed to detect the attack for about two months.

breaches.cost_type: Ransom payment reported by the Wall Street Journal; company implied payment in SEC filing without confirming the figure
breaches.records_note: Loyalty program database with driver's licenses and Social Security numbers; total count not disclosed
breaches.what_happened: Attackers used social engineering to trick an outsourced IT help desk into resetting credentials, then stole the Caesars loyalty program database containing driver's license and Social Security numbers. Caesars implied in its SEC filing that it negotiated with the attackers to have the stolen data deleted, a step widely interpreted as a ransom payment.

breaches.cost_type: Ransom payment confirmed by the company (June 2021)
breaches.records_note: Company reported no customer, supplier, or employee data was compromised
breaches.what_happened: The REvil ransomware group hit JBS USA's IT network in May 2021, temporarily shutting down meat processing plants in the US, Canada, and Australia. The company restored operations quickly from backups but paid the ransom to guard against data exfiltration and protect customers.

breaches.cost_type: Ransom paid in Bitcoin (May 2021); DOJ recovered ~$2.3 million
breaches.records_note: 5,810 individuals notified; about 100GB of data claimed stolen by the attackers
breaches.what_happened: DarkSide ransomware affiliates gained access through a legacy VPN account that lacked multi-factor authentication, encrypting Colonial's corporate IT network. The company shut down pipeline operations for five days as a precaution, triggering fuel shortages across the southeastern US, and the DOJ later recovered about half the ransom from the attackers' wallet.

breaches.cost_type: SEC civil penalty for misleading disclosures (August 2021)
breaches.records_note: Millions of rows of student data and admin credentials across 13,000 customer accounts; exact individual count not disclosed
breaches.what_happened: Attackers exploited a critical vulnerability Pearson had left unpatched for six months, stealing millions of student records and administrator login credentials across 13,000 school, district, and university customer accounts. The SEC found Pearson described the incident as a hypothetical risk in filings and understated its scope in public statements.

breaches.cost_type: Ransom payment reported by Wired; company did not confirm the figure
breaches.records_note: Call and text metadata for about 110 million customers
breaches.what_happened: Threat actors used stolen credentials to access AT&T's Snowflake cloud data warehouse, which lacked multi-factor authentication, and downloaded call and text metadata for nearly all customers. AT&T delayed public disclosure at the FBI's request and reportedly paid the hackers to delete the stolen data.

metadata.currency_note: All figures converted to US dollars. The British Airways fine was levied in pounds (£20 million) and is converted at approximately 1.30.
metadata.description: Notable publicly reported breach and incident costs, 2018-2026, with related SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria. Educational aid only.
metadata.figure_note: Figures are reported costs, settlements, fines, or ransom payments from the cited sources. They are not predictions and do not include unreported response costs, lost business, or litigation beyond what is cited.
